intended_object: A zero object in a category: an object that is both initial and terminal, i.e. for every object Y there is exactly one morphism X → Y and exactly one morphism Y → X. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The structure asks, for every object Y, for `Nonempty (Unique (X ⟶ Y))` and `Nonempty (Unique (Y ⟶ X))`. This says exactly that each hom-set to and from X has one element, so X is both initial and terminal. That is the standard definition of a zero object. It works in any category and needs no extra hypotheses, so it is stated at its natural generality. In the degenerate case of the empty category the condition holds vacuously, but there is no object X to apply it to, so this changes nothing. This declaration is Mathlib's own definition of the notion, so there is no other Mathlib definition to cite as a counterpart.
